You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

    else: return [i[:,k*i.shape[0]: (k+1)*i.shape[0]] for k in range(i.shape[1]//i.shape[0])]

    bls=blocks_of(i); ch=next(j for j,b in enumerate(bls) if np.array_equal(b,o))
    f=[]
    for b in bls:
        a=np.array(b); n=b.shape[0]
        c=np.bincount(a.ravel().tolist()); mx=c.max()
        # repeated adjacent pairs
        p=sum(int((a[r,c]==a[r,c+1]).all()) for r in range(n) for c in range(n-1)) + sum(int((a[r,c]==a[r+1,c]).all()) for r in range(n-1) for c in range(n))
        rep_rows=sum(1 for r in range(n) if len(set(a[r].tolist()))==1)

        diag=sum(1 for r in range(n) for c in range(n-1) if a[r,c]==a[r+1,c+1])
        anti=sum(1 for r in range(n) for c in range(n-1) if a[r,c]==a[r+1,c-1])
        pal=int(np.array_equal(np.fliplr(a),a)); pud=int(np.array_equal(np.flipud(a),a))

    print(name,rows,'argmax',[f.index(max(r)) for r in rows],'CHON' if [idx for idx,v in []] else '')

import numpy as np, json
pairs=[(np.array(G['Demo pair %d input'%k]),np.array(G['Demo pair %d output'%k])) for k in range(1,8)]
def blocks_of(i):
    if i.shape[0]>i.shape[1]: return [i[k*i.shape[1]: (k+1)*i.shape[1]] for k in range(i.shape[0]//i.shape[1])]
    else: return [i[:,k*i.shape[0]: (k+1)*i.shape[0]] for k in range(i.shape[1]//i.shape[0])]
def f(i):
    bls=blocks_of(i)
    asym=[j for j,b in enumerate(bls) if not np.array_equal(np.array(b),b.T)]
    # sanity: exactly one should be asymmetric in every demo
    assert len(asym)==1,(asym,)
    return bls[asym[0]].tolist()
ok=all(f(i)==o.tolist() for i,o in pairs)
print('all demos match:',ok)
T=np.array(G['Test input']); out=f(T); print(json.dumps(out))
